questions.question: How can you check if a vehicle built before 1998 has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes. This tells you if the trailer has ABS.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: It sends air to the trailer.
It turns off the air brakes.
It keeps the vehicle from skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It sends air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too fast.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel quickly left, then right.

questions.explanation: Release the brakes so the wheels can grip the road again. The trailer will straighten out once traction returns.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification mean?

options.text: The amount of noise at the back of a vehicle.
How many trailers a tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can rollover because of the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification.

questions.question: When connecting a trailer, what should you do with the glad hands?

options.text: Leave one pair of glad hands loose.

questions.explanation: Connect only the matching pairs of glad hands when connecting air brake hoses. They are sometimes color-coded. Blue is usually for service lines and red for emergency lines.

questions.question: When glad hands are connected, the seals should touch at what angle?
questions.explanation: When connecting glad hands, press the seals together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line supply air to?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: How should you use the brakes in a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
While the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Use the brakes the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: If a trailer starts to jackknife, what should the driver do?

options.text: Do not apply the trailer hand brake.
Use the parking brake to straighten the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: Release the brakes and let the wheels regain traction. Do not use the trailer hand brake because applying brakes is what locked the wheels in the first place.

questions.question: What is rearward amplification?

options.text: The noise coming from the back of the vehicle.
The cause of the crack-the-whip effect.
The number of trailers one tractor can pull.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cause of the crack-the-whip effect.
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the crack-the-whip effect. If not handled properly, a trailer can tip over because of rearward amplification.

questions.question: If you press the tractor air supply control and the trailer's spring brakes do not release, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: All vehicle equipment must work properly before you drive. If the trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, check that the air line connections are tight and properly sealed.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what is most important?

options.text: Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.explanation: Improper coupling and uncoupling can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow it.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a trailer. Bobtail tractors are hard to control, so drivers must be careful.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator hard when starting.

questions.explanation: Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, where should the air supply control lever be?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles use levers instead of knobs for the tractor protection control. The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while the vehicle is moving can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer during coupling, what should you do next?
questions.explanation: Follow the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers safely. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, you should supply air to it.
